title: Event bus service in Node.js
idea: A Node.js event bus service writes each event to an outbox table in the business transaction; a relay publishes it, and subscribers dedupe.
points: The order and its outbox row commit together, so no event is lost.
A relay locks unpublished rows in id order, delivers them, then marks them.
A crash before marking redelivers; the `processed_event` inbox makes repeats harmless.
Follow-ups: partition the outbox by key, one relay each, or a real broker.

messages.label: POST /orders + key
messages.note: The request carries an Idempotency-Key, so a retried click cannot create two orders.

messages.label: order + outbox row
messages.note: One transaction inserts both rows. Either both commit or neither does.

messages.label: 201 order
messages.note: The client gets its answer without waiting for any subscriber.

messages.label: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
messages.note: The relay locks unpublished rows in id order. A second relay would skip them and could reorder a key.

messages.label: deliver event
messages.note: Each subscriber receives the event with its outbox id.

messages.label: inbox row + points
messages.note: The subscriber records the event id and applies its effect in one transaction.

messages.label: crash before marking
messages.note: The relay crashes before setting published_at, so the rows stay unpublished.

messages.label: redeliver
messages.note: The inbox insert conflicts, so the subscriber skips the repeat.

code.title: Outbox relay on PostgreSQL
code.caption: An Express order API with an outbox, a relay that crashes once on purpose, and an inbox that absorbs the redelivery.

walk.text: Orders with a unique key, the outbox, the inbox table and a loyalty balance.
The in-process bus: a map from topic to subscriber functions.
One transaction writes the order and its outbox row; a replay returns the stored order.
The relay locks unpublished rows by id, delivers, marks them. Ids follow insert order, not commit order.
Email has no dedupe. Loyalty records the event id and adds points together.
The controller checks the key and validates with zod; middleware maps errors to codes.
Create, replay, reused key, missing key, bad body; then a relay crash and two reruns.

pitfalls: Never publish to a broker inside the request before commit; a rollback leaves a ghost event.
Subscribers without an inbox, like email here, repeat their side effects on redelivery.
Two SKIP LOCKED relays can reorder one key; give each relay its own key partition.

quiz.q: What does the last line of the service demo print?
quiz.why: The crashed relay still delivered both events, and loyalty committed them. On redelivery the inbox insert conflicts, so points are added once: 250 plus 120.

takeaway: Outbox in the same transaction, relay at least once, inbox to dedupe.

starters: How would I scale the relay without losing per-key order?
When should I replace the outbox relay with Kafka or another broker?
Could LISTEN and NOTIFY replace polling the outbox table?
